items.title: 68190_Samuel
items.q: they didn't know anything about and that goes for Johnny Hodges and all the guys

ctx.x: Crook Goodwin and Art Smith here at the Afterhours in Kansas City. The end of Side One of this Tape Three we were discussing Lester Young and I referred briefly to Charlie Parker. I think now I'd like to go back to Charlie Parker and get your opinion, Baby, and later yours, Crook, on Charlie Parker and the whole Charlie Parker almost-mythology that's grown up about him. Baby, what do you know about Charlie Parker? When did you meet him, what did you think of him, how well did you know him?

I knew him pretty well. He lived a couple of blocks from me on 16th Street, Kansas City, Missouri, and when he first left here and went to New York, he was so far ahead of the alto players playing then that the guys laughed at him for playing so much out that they didn't know anything about and that goes for Johnny Hodges and all the guys.

They would sit around and listen to him and didn't want him to know they were out there. He was playing so much stuff that they couldn't play it, you understand what I mean, and that's where he made his fame in New York there. They finally got used to his playing, man, and everybody tried to play like Charlie Parker, which you know that.
